_comment: Bias jury contract. Jurors answer yes/no per item and must cite IDs for every 'no'. Votes are combined in plain Python (app/jury/aggregate.py), never by an LLM.

normalization.title: Normalized requirements vs. the raw SRS

items.question: Is every requirement stated in the RAW SRS represented in the NORMALIZED REQUIREMENTS?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the raw SRS line numbers (e.g. L4) of each requirement that was dropped
items.fix: Requirements stated in the raw SRS are missing from the normalized list

items.question: Is every NORMALIZED REQUIREMENT supported by something the RAW SRS actually says (nothing invented or exaggerated)?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the requirement IDs (e.g. NFR-002) that the raw SRS does not support
items.fix: These normalized requirements are not supported by the raw SRS; remove or correct them

items.question: Is every requirement marked ASR backed by an explicit RAW SRS statement about scale, latency, consistency, availability, security, deployment or cost?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the ASR IDs that were promoted without such a statement
items.fix: These requirements were promoted to ASR without an explicit architectural driver in the raw SRS

items.question: Is every ASR actually realized by at least one COMPONENT in the architecture?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the ASR IDs that no component realizes
items.fix: These ASRs are not realized by any component

items.question: Is the chosen ARCHITECTURAL STYLE compatible with every ASR?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the ASR IDs the style conflicts with
items.fix: The architectural style conflicts with these ASRs

items.question: Is every technology component (message broker, cache, queue, gateway, orchestrator, search engine) required by a requirement, rather than added because it is popular?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the component IDs (e.g. COMP-004) that no requirement needs
items.fix: These components are not required by any requirement; remove them or justify them with a requirement

items.question: Are the number and granularity of COMPONENTS proportionate to the scale stated in the requirements (no over-engineering)?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the component IDs that are unnecessary splits or excess infrastructure
items.fix: These components over-engineer the system for its stated scale; merge or remove them

items.question: Does every CONNECTION represent a real call or data flow that a requirement needs?
items.cite_help: for 'no', cite the connection IDs (e.g. EDGE-003) that no requirement needs
items.fix: These connections are not needed by any requirement
